name: Joshaphat
overview: Joshaphat was a male figure known as the Mithnite, a designation that identifies him uniquely in Scripture. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional notes about his life. His mention is brief but distinct, marking him as a noteworthy individual in the biblical record.
namesAndTitles: The name Joshaphat means 'YHWH judges,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that highlights God's sovereign judgment. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 11:43 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Joshaphat was the son of Hanan, as noted in 1 Chronicles 11:43. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded, and no further familial details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Joshaphat's significance lies in his identification as the Mithnite, which sets him apart among the warriors or notable men listed in the chronicled genealogies. Though details about his deeds are not given, his inclusion in the biblical record underscores the faithfulness of God’s people and the importance of those who served under His providence. His name's meaning further points believers to the sovereignty of God’s judgment in the lives of His servants.
